review_scope: Different-author static and synthetic-only review of the exact committed M1628 source, tests, contract and author receipt. No actual ep34 payload was opened; no actual L2/L3 execution, attempt, release, GPU or EDA work occurred.

evidence: CanonicalPrefixMiter.configuration remains directly mutable after all requests and destination states have been accepted.
The hidden issued-session registry stores only identity to owner, not identity to immutable initial configuration.
Three distinct sessions were all executed as DENSE_TYPED_K8, then the second and third owners were relabelled to BIT_EQUAL_SERVICE_K1X8 and BIT_TYPED_K8 immediately before finish.
All three genuine HMAC receipts had distinct fresh session identities and the expected reported configuration order, while all three retained dense-only coverage flags.
validate_bundle accepted this relabelled bundle, so it does not prove that the three required configurations actually executed in different fresh sessions.
p1.required_repair: At session creation, bind (exact owner, immutable initial configuration) in the hidden issued registry; require that bound configuration at every request/state/finish and in the authenticated payload. In validate_bundle, require the exact per-configuration coverage policy, including false dense-only flags for both bit configurations. Add this exact relabel attack to the successor dual-runtime tests.

p2.finding: RSS is validated independently for both rows but remains outside PREFIX_EXACT_FIELDS, as already disclosed by M1620.
p2.disposition: Keep the comparison policy explicit in the future runner/result receipt; do not present RSS equality as part of L2 functional exactness.

single_next_action: Author a separately named source-only successor that immutably binds initial configuration in the hidden session registry and rejects the reproduced relabel attack; obtain another different-author review with P0=0/P1=0 before any actual runner source or M1633 release.
